text: A new C++ ground node fits the floor plane from the 10 Hz ToF cloud with an IMU prior and gives plane-relative obstacle, step and drop-off marks; only real data is published.

The plane-relative marks feed Nav2 alongside the current fixed bands (switch-over only after validation, criteria documented); the collision monitor keeps the 10 Hz ToF; the global costmap stays static + lidar; no depth-bias correction in this epic.
The ground estimate (floor height, slope with the tilt_guard cross-check, steps and drop-offs as surface regions) is available to consumers: mcp_server map summary and floor_guard Terrain.
RGB-D colour labels floor vs obstacle, and the ground estimate is visible in the web UI map.
Ansible node type with the ros2_nodes schema and a cgroup tier, metrics with a Grafana panel, and the CPU budget measured on the Pi 5.
READMEs, tests/README.md, MEMORY entry, runbook and a final robot verification executed after merge.

Obstacle vs warning rule (replaces Q1): a step, threshold, drop or ramp cluster is an OBSTACLE (lethal: its points go to /ground/obstacle_points or /ground/drop_points and the ground_voxel_layer) when its edge step exceeds one third of the wheel diameter (traversability.wheel_radius_m 0.06 from swerve_drive_controller wheel_radius_m, max_step_fraction 1/3 -> 0.04 m, configurable, pinned equal by a consistency test) or its surface slope exceeds traversability.max_slope_deg (default 8 deg, my call: the lower of the tilt_guard warn limits, roll 8 / pitch 12, because a swerve base can meet a ramp at any heading, so driving onto a steeper ramp would at once raise a tilt_guard warning); otherwise it is a WARNING area, clear to ride through at reduced speed. Colour-flagged flat objects (floor_colour_mismatch clusters) are classified by the same rule. Tests cover both sides of each threshold (0.035/0.045 m sills and drops, 6/10 deg ramps, exactly 0.04 m and 8 deg are warnings).
